tasks.title: Query plan: viewing
tasks.statement: EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN shows how the database will run a query. Show the plan for `SELECT * FROM customers WHERE city = 'Москва'`. There is no index on city, so it will be a SCAN, a full pass.
tasks.hint: Put EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN in front of the ordinary query.
tasks.starter:
-- add EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN
SELECT * FROM customers WHERE city = 'Москва';

tasks.title: Plan: lookup by key
tasks.statement: Show the plan for SELECT * FROM customers WHERE id = 5. A primary key gives a fast lookup (SEARCH … INTEGER PRIMARY KEY).

tasks.title: Plan: composite key
tasks.statement: order_items has a composite primary key (order_id, product_id). Show the plan for a query on both columns: WHERE order_id = 5 AND product_id = 7. The plan will use the automatic index sqlite_autoindex_order_items_1.

tasks.title: Plan: second key column
tasks.statement: The index of a composite key works only on its leading column. Show the plan for SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE product_id = 3. The result will be a full scan, SCAN.

tasks.title: The first index
tasks.statement: The query `SELECT * FROM customers WHERE city = 'Москва'` scans the table. Create an index on city so that the plan becomes a SEARCH.

tasks.title: Index on a foreign key
tasks.statement: Create an index that speeds up SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 5.

tasks.title: Index on status
tasks.statement: Create an index for the query `SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'new'`.

tasks.title: Composite index
tasks.statement: The query: WHERE customer_id = 5 AND status = 'paid'. Create one composite index on (customer_id, status) so that both columns take part in the lookup.

tasks.title: Equality and range
tasks.statement: The query: WHERE customer_id = 5 AND created > '2024-04-01'. Create an index on (customer_id, created): equality first, range second.
tasks.hint: Put columns with equality before the column with a range.

tasks.title: Index for ORDER BY
tasks.statement: The query SELECT * FROM products ORDER BY price sorts in a temporary structure (USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY). Create an index on price so that no sort is needed.
tasks.hint: An index stores the values already sorted.

tasks.title: Filter and sort
tasks.statement: The query: WHERE category = `'Электроника'` ORDER BY price. Create an index on (category, price) so that there is neither a scan nor a sort.

tasks.title: Covering index
tasks.statement: The query SELECT customer_id, status, total FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 5 reads only three columns. Create a covering index on (customer_id, status, total); the plan must contain COVERING INDEX.

tasks.title: Index for a JOIN
tasks.statement: The query: SELECT * FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE p.category = `'Книги'`. Create an index so that order_items is read by a SEARCH on product_id.
tasks.hint: Index the join column in the table that is searched.

tasks.title: Unique index
tasks.statement: Create a unique index on customer email (any number of NULLs is allowed): CREATE UNIQUE INDEX. The unique flag is checked.
tasks.hint: A unique index also forbids duplicates.

tasks.title: Partial index
tasks.statement: Only a small part of the orders have the status `'new'`. Create a partial index on created for the rows WHERE status = `'new'`, which is more compact than an ordinary one. The check is that a query on new uses the index.
tasks.hint: The query must contain the same condition status = `'new'`.

tasks.title: Expression index
tasks.statement: The query WHERE lower(email) = 'anna@mail.ru' does not use the index on email. Create an index on the expression lower(email).

tasks.title: Prefix search
tasks.statement: The query: title GLOB `'Книга*'` (the start of a string). Create an index on title. A GLOB with a constant beginning uses the index as a range.

tasks.title: A function kills the index
tasks.statement: There is an index on orders(created). The query with a function WHERE strftime('%Y', created) = '2024' does not use it. Rewrite the condition as a range on created (from '2024-01-01' to '2024-12-31' inclusive) and show the plan of your query with EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN.
tasks.hint: Do not wrap the column in a function: compare the column itself with the bounds.

tasks.title: OR via UNION ALL
tasks.statement: The query WHERE customer_id = 5 OR status = 'new' uses indexes poorly. The setup has indexes on customer_id and status; rewrite the query as a UNION ALL of two selects and show its plan (EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN). Two SEARCH lines are needed.

tasks.title: Leading column
tasks.statement: There is an index on (customer_id, status). The query WHERE status = 'new' cannot use its leading column. Create an additional index on (status) so that the plan becomes a SEARCH on status.

tasks.title: DISTINCT via an index
tasks.statement: Create an index after which SELECT DISTINCT city FROM customers runs without a temporary structure (TEMP B-TREE).

tasks.title: GROUP BY via an index
tasks.statement: Create an index after which SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id needs no temporary sort (TEMP B-TREE FOR GROUP BY).

tasks.title: MAX via an index
tasks.statement: Create an index that speeds up SELECT MAX(price) FROM products down to reading a single value (the plan shows SEARCH … COVERING INDEX).

tasks.title: Leading LIKE pattern
tasks.statement: A pattern with % at the start (`LIKE '%книга'`) does not use an index: show the plan for `SELECT * FROM products WHERE title LIKE '%Книга'` with an index on title. The result will be a SCAN.

tasks.title: Unused index
tasks.statement: The orders table has an index idx_orders_old that nobody needs: drop it (DROP INDEX). The check looks at the list of manually created indexes.

tasks.title: Duplicate index
tasks.statement: The index idx_a (customer_id) is a prefix of the index idx_b (customer_id, status), so it is redundant. Drop idx_a.

tasks.title: ANALYZE statistics
tasks.statement: Gather statistics for the optimizer (ANALYZE). The check is that sqlite_stat1 now has rows for the indexes of orders.

tasks.title: Which indexes exist
tasks.statement: Show the names of the manually created indexes of the orders table (pragma_index_list, origin = 'c'); ordered by name.

tasks.title: Index columns
tasks.statement: Show the columns of the index idx_orders_cust_status in order: pragma_index_info('idx_orders_cust_status'), columns seqno, name; ordered by seqno.

tasks.title: Column selectivity
tasks.statement: The more distinct values, the more selective the column. For orders show the share of distinct values: status_sel = COUNT(DISTINCT status) * 1.0 / COUNT(*), customer_sel for customer_id, total_sel for total; ROUND to 2 decimal places.
tasks.hint: An index on a column with few values (status) is of little use.

tasks.title: Tables without manual indexes
tasks.statement: Show the names of tables that have no manually created index at all (origin = 'c'); ordered by name. Use sqlite_master and pragma_index_list.

tasks.title: Indexes and keys
tasks.statement: Show the tables of the database and the number of indexes on each (including the automatic ones for PRIMARY KEY and UNIQUE): name, idx_count; ordered by name.

tasks.title: Page by key
tasks.statement: Show the next page of 5 orders after id = 8 without OFFSET: id, total; WHERE id > 8 ORDER BY id LIMIT 5. The cost does not depend on the page number.

tasks.title: Covering index and plan
tasks.statement: The setup has an index on (customer_id). Create a covering index idx_cover on (customer_id, created) and show the plan for SELECT created FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 3. The plan must contain COVERING INDEX idx_cover.
